items.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: like hear Snooky Young play. Or Sweets Edison.

ctx.x: It keeps going around, you know.

If acoustic stays out long enough, it might be the new thing in a while, you know, if people get enough of digitally produced sounds, they might—if they hear guys, like hear Snooky Young play. Or Sweets Edison. Did you happen to hear him play?
We talked to him. We didn’t get to hear him.

items.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: it was very nice, man, I enjoyed working with them.

ctx.x: But, it would be the same thing. They would rehearse the act‘s music, the act‘s. And some acts come in there with some tough music and some acts it was just, one time and you go it, but you know. But, it would be, it was nice, it was difficult too. It was good, but you had to be able to do it. All of the musicians, all of them was, had to read that music, and had to be able to play that music, whatever they brought in, and they brought everything in, all kinds of music in, you know what I‘m saying. All kinds of…
